raw_annotations.proposed_function: Self-assembly and phase separation via multivalent interactions
raw_annotations.evidence: Its disordered C-terminal low-complexity domain (LCD, residues 267–414), rich in glycine, glutamine/asparagine, and serine, bears features of a prion-like region and plays a central role in self-assembly of the protein and in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases [ 3, 4 ].

raw_annotations.proposed_function: Mediates liquid-liquid phase separation and micelle formation through self-assembly into droplets and nanoparticles
raw_annotations.evidence: At 150 mM NaCl and 50 μM total protein, the unphosphorylated LCD rapidly assembled into a dense population of micron-scale fluorescent spherical droplets, already abundant within a few minutes of sample loading (Figure 3d ).
raw_annotations.curator_note: Exact positions not provided; suggest UniProt canonical lookup for TDP-43 LCD coordinates.

raw_annotations.evidence: To compare the phase-separation propensities of phosphorylated and unphosphorylated TDP-43 LCD, turbidity measurements were performed in parallel on three samples: (i) CK1 δ- phosphorylated TDP-43 LCD (phLCD); (ii) “aged” unphosphorylated TDP-43 LCD (non-phLCD prepared in parallel with phLCD without kinase and ATP, allowed to age for the same duration); and (iii) “freshly” prepared non-phLCD.
raw_annotations.curator_note: Qualitative mention only; exact residue coordinates not provided in the text. Suggest UniProt canonical lookup for TDP-43 LCD boundaries.

raw_annotations.evidence: No quantitative image analysis was performed; the imaging served as direct optical confirmation of TDP-43 LCD phase separation and coalescence kinetics in the unphosphorylated state, as well as direct evidence for the suppression of phase separation in the phosphorylated state.
